components.note: 大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
口 (mouth) — 号 relates to calling or crying out aloud, as well as a spoken or marked sign
丂 gives a loose sound connection to 号's reading hào

example.hanzi: 他是公司里的头号员工。
example.pinyin: tā shì gōngsī lǐ de tóuhào yuángōng.
example.english: He is the top-ranked employee in the company.
example.fact: Mount Everest, straddling the border between Nepal and Tibet, holds the top rank among Earth's peaks at 8,849 meters — its height was last officially remeasured by a joint Chinese-Nepali survey in 2020, using GPS and gravity data instead of the purely trigonometric methods used a century earlier.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match
彡 (hair/decorative strokes) — 修 relates to grooming, decorating, or improving something
攸 (yōu) gives a sound close to 修's reading xiū, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 他们打算重新装修厨房。
example.pinyin: tāmen dǎsuàn chóngxīn zhuāngxiū chúfáng.
example.english: They plan to renovate the kitchen.
example.fact: Antoni Gaudí's Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882 and remains unfinished — architects today use 3D-printed models and computer simulations to complete Gaudí's original hand-carved plaster designs, with completion now targeted for the 2030s.

components.note: 亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'
土 here is a worn-down form of 大, a person — in the oracle-bone form of 去, a figure is shown stepping away from an opening.
厶 represents a pit or opening the figure above is moving away from, giving 去 its meaning 'to leave, to go.'

example.hanzi: 火车即将离去。
example.pinyin: huǒchē jíjiāng líqù.
example.english: The train is about to leave.
example.fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway, completed in 1916, is the longest railway line in the world at over 9,289 kilometers, connecting Moscow to Vladivostok — a nonstop journey along its full length takes about six days.

components.note: 门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.
覀 here depicts rising flames.
示 (altar) — burning paper offerings over an altar, a traditional practice, gave 票 its meaning of a paper note, later 'ticket, banknote.'

example.hanzi: 我买了两张电影门票。
example.pinyin: wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng diànyǐng ménpiào.
example.english: I bought two movie tickets.
example.fact: The Lumière brothers held the world's first paid public film screening on December 28, 1895, in the basement of the Grand Café in Paris — admission cost one franc, and the ten short films shown that night reportedly startled early audiences unused to moving pictures.

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 反 pictures pushing against a steep surface.
又 (a hand) — a hand pushing back against a cliff gave 反 its meaning 'to turn over' or 'opposite.'
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'

example.hanzi: 军队发起了反击。
example.pinyin: jūnduì fāqǐ le fǎnjī.
example.english: The army launched a counterattack.
example.fact: During the Battle of Midway in June 1942, American dive bombers launched a decisive counterattack that sank four Japanese aircraft carriers in a single day — historians consider it the turning point of the Pacific theater in World War II.

meanings: to open (a new road or railway line)

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 这条地铁线路刚刚开通。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo dìtiě xiànlù gānggāng kāitōng.
example.english: This subway line has just opened.
example.fact: The London Underground, opened in 1863, is the world's oldest underground railway network — its first section, the Metropolitan Railway, ran steam locomotives through gas-lit tunnels decades before electric trains were introduced in 1890.

components.note: 日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.
艹 (grass/plant) — 落 relates to leaves or plants falling
洛 (luò) gives the sound — 落 is also pronounced luò, an exact match

example.hanzi: 我们坐在海边看日落。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zuò zài hǎibiān kàn rìluò.
example.english: We sat by the sea watching the sunset.
example.fact: Sunsets appear orange and red because sunlight travels through more of the atmosphere at a low angle, scattering away shorter blue wavelengths through a process called Rayleigh scattering and leaving the longer red and orange wavelengths to reach our eyes.

components.note: 冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'
心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.
十 (ten, suggesting abundance) — relates to 华's meaning 'flowery, splendid,' an abundance of blossoms.
化 (huà) gives a sound hint — 华 is pronounced huá, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 爱德华是我的朋友。
example.pinyin: àidéhuá shì wǒ de péngyou.
example.english: Edward is my friend.
example.fact: Edward Jenner, an English physician, developed the world's first vaccine in 1796 by inoculating a boy with cowpox material to protect him against smallpox — his work laid the foundation for modern immunology and eventually led to smallpox's global eradication in 1980.

meanings: middle ranking officer in Chinese army

components.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
木 (wood) — 校 originally related to a wooden framework, later coming to mean 'school,' a place of structured learning
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 校's reading xiào

example.hanzi: 他去年晋升为中校。
example.pinyin: tā qùnián jìnshēng wéi zhōngxiào.
example.english: He was promoted to lieutenant colonel last year.
example.fact: The military rank of colonel derives from the Italian word 'colonna,' meaning column, since a colonel originally commanded a column of troops — the rank spread across European armies during the 16th century as standing professional forces replaced feudal levies.

components.note: 彡 (fine lines) — suggests light and shadow, relating to 影's meaning 'shadow, image.'
景 (jǐng) gives a sound hint — 影 is pronounced yǐng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 阳光下,他的影子很长。
example.pinyin: yángguāng xià, tā de yǐngzi hěn cháng.
example.english: In the sunlight, his shadow is very long.
example.fact: Around 240 BC, the Greek scholar Eratosthenes calculated Earth's circumference by comparing the length of a shadow cast by a stick in Alexandria to reports of no shadow at noon in Syene, modern Aswan — his estimate came within about 5 to 15 percent of the true value.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 没 originally meant to sink or drown in water, later extended to the negative 'not have.'
殳 (shū) is the historical sound component; it no longer rhymes with méi in modern Mandarin, another case of sound drift over time.
钅 (metal/gold) — represents something valuable.
昔 (formerly, in the past) — valuable metal that has been mishandled or lost over time gave 错 its meaning 'mistake, wrong.'

example.hanzi: “你说得没错。”他点点头说。
example.pinyin: “nǐ shuō de méicuò.” tā diǎndiǎntóu shuō.
example.english: "You're right," he said, nodding.
example.fact: Nodding to signal agreement is common across most cultures, but naturalist Charles Darwin noted in 1872 that some communities in Bulgaria, Greece, and parts of the Middle East traditionally used the opposite gesture — a head shake — to mean yes, a reversal anthropologists still debate the origins of.

components.note: 户 (door) — 居 relates to where one lives, behind a door
古 (gǔ) gives a sound related to 居's reading jū, from an older, closer pronunciation link
亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'

example.hanzi: 很多人居住在城市里。
example.pinyin: hěn duō rén jūzhù zài chéngshì lǐ.
example.english: Many people reside in cities.
example.fact: In 2007, the United Nations reported that, for the first time in human history, more than half of the world's population lived in urban areas rather than rural ones — a share projected to reach roughly 68 percent by 2050.

components.note: 卫 is a simplified form derived from the cursive shorthand of the traditional character 衛, which pictured a foot patrolling around a guarded, walled area; the simplification collapsed these parts into a single compact shape that no longer breaks into separately readable pieces, while keeping 衛's meaning 'to guard, defend.'
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
门 (door/gate) — 间 pictures light passing through an entryway.
日 (sun) — sunlight shining through a gap in a doorway gave 间 its meaning of a space 'in between,' as in 中间 (in the middle) or 时间 (time, the space between moments).

example.hanzi: 卫生间在走廊尽头。
example.pinyin: wèishēngjiān zài zǒuláng jìntóu.
example.english: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
example.fact: The modern flush toilet was patented in 1775 by Scottish inventor Alexander Cumming, who added the S-shaped trap that uses standing water to block sewer odors — a design principle still used in almost every toilet today.

components.note: 冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.

方 is a pictograph of an ancient plow with a handle and crossbar. The character was later borrowed phonetically to write the unrelated meanings 'square' and 'direction,' a common process in Chinese character history known as phonetic loan.

example.hanzi: 军方否认了这一说法。
example.pinyin: jūnfāng fǒurèn le zhè yī shuōfǎ.
example.english: The military denied this claim.
example.fact: GPS was originally developed by the United States military in the 1970s to guide missiles and ships, and it wasn't opened for full-precision civilian use until 2000, after President Clinton ordered the removal of intentional signal degradation.

components.note: 戊 is a pictograph of an ancient dagger-axe or halberd. The addition of a short stroke through the blade suggested a weapon completed and ready for use, which extended metaphorically to 成's meanings 'to complete, to become, to succeed.'
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

example.hanzi: 请检查一下这个产品的成分。
example.pinyin: qǐng jiǎnchá yíxià zhège chǎnpǐn de chéngfèn.
example.english: Please check the ingredients of this product.
example.fact: Earth's atmosphere is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen by volume, with the remaining roughly 1 percent made up of argon, carbon dioxide, and trace gases — a composition that has stayed fairly stable for hundreds of millions of years thanks to photosynthesis replenishing oxygen.

components.note: 其 is a pictograph of a woven winnowing basket, seen from above with its rim and base visible — a meaning today written with the added 竹 (bamboo) radical as 箕. The basket character was borrowed phonetically to write the common pronoun and demonstrative 'its, that,' its usual meaning now.
冫 (originally a mark for repetition, unrelated to its later meaning 'ice') — suggests something done more than once.
欠 (a person yawning, mouth open) — repeated yawning gave 次 its meaning of a 'time' or occurrence, as in counting how many times something happens.

example.hanzi: 首先要准备材料,其次是开始施工。
example.pinyin: shǒuxiān yào zhǔnbèi cáiliào, qící shì kāishǐ shīgōng.
example.english: First you need to prepare the materials, and secondly begin construction.
example.fact: The Pantheon in Rome, completed around 128 AD, still holds the record for the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome — Roman engineers achieved this partly by using a lighter volcanic aggregate, pumice, in the concrete near the top of the dome.

components.note: 另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.
野 (open countryside) — 墅 names a house set in the countryside.
土 (tǔ) gives a sound distantly related to 墅's reading shù, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他们在海边买了一座别墅。
example.pinyin: tāmen zài hǎibiān mǎi le yī zuò biéshù.
example.english: They bought a villa by the seaside.
example.fact: Many Roman aristocrats built lavish seaside villas along the Bay of Naples, and the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD preserved several of them, including the Villa of the Papyri near Herculaneum, buried under volcanic ash so completely that its wall paintings and carbonized scrolls survived nearly 2,000 years.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 艾 names a plant, mugwort.
乂 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to ài, having drifted apart over time.
辶 (walk/movement) — 迪 describes moving forward.
由 (a source, a path from) — walking 辶 from a clear starting point 由 gave 迪 its meaning 'to guide, to enlighten.'

example.hanzi: 艾迪是我们班最高的学生。
example.pinyin: àidí shì wǒmen bān zuì gāo de xuésheng.
example.english: Eddie is the tallest student in our class.
example.fact: British ski jumper Michael 'Eddie the Eagle' Edwards became a folk hero at the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics by finishing last in his event despite minimal training — his popularity led the International Olympic Committee to later tighten qualifying standards, informally nicknamed the 'Eddie the Eagle rule.'

components.note: 凵 depicts an open container or pit, shown here holding something dangerous inside.
乂 is a crossed mark suggesting something tangled or harmful — trapped inside the container 凵, it gives 凶 its meaning 'vicious, ominous.'
乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查一起凶杀案。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá yī qǐ xiōngshā àn.
example.english: The police are investigating a murder case.
example.fact: Fingerprint identification became a standard forensic tool after Argentine police officer Juan Vucetich used it to solve a murder case in Necochea in 1892, matching a bloody fingerprint at the scene to the suspect — it was the first murder conviction secured primarily through fingerprint evidence.

components.note: 网 depicts a woven mesh net stretched over a frame — a picture of a fishing or hunting net, giving 网 its meaning 'net, network.'
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match

example.hanzi: 她每周打两次网球。
example.pinyin: tā měi zhōu dǎ liǎng cì wǎngqiú.
example.english: She plays tennis twice a week.
example.fact: Wimbledon, first held in 1877 on a single grass court in London, is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and the only Grand Slam event still played on grass — its groundskeepers mow the courts to a precise height of 8 millimeters.

components.note: 口 (mouth) on top represents speaking or presenting something.
王 (a king) below shows who the words are presented to, giving 呈 its meaning 'to submit, to present.'
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — a valuable object one might glimpse or notice.
见 (to see) — catching sight of something links to the meanings 'to appear, present, now.'

example.hanzi: 数据呈现出明显的上升趋势。
example.pinyin: shùjù chéngxiàn chū míngxiǎn de shàngshēng qūshì.
example.english: The data shows a clear upward trend.
example.fact: In 1965, Intel co-founder Gordon Moore observed that the number of transistors on a computer chip tended to double roughly every two years, a trend now known as Moore's Law — it held remarkably well for over five decades before physical limits began to slow it in the 2020s.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
小 (small, young) — 叔 describes a younger member of the family.
又 (a hand) — historically part of a scene of picking beans; today it simply combines with 小 to give 叔 its meaning 'a younger uncle.'

example.hanzi: 那个大叔每天早上都在公园锻炼。
example.pinyin: nàge dàshū měitiān zǎoshang dōu zài gōngyuán duànliàn.
example.english: That older man exercises in the park every morning.
example.fact: Researchers studying so-called 'Blue Zones' — regions like Okinawa, Japan, and Sardinia, Italy, with unusually high numbers of centenarians — found that daily low-intensity movement such as walking and gardening, rather than intense exercise, is one of the strongest shared habits among people who live past 100.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诺 relates to a spoken promise or agreement.
若 (ruò) gives a rhyme close to nuò, sharing a related initial.
口 (mouth) — with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out — the image of speaking, the source of 言's meaning 'speech, words, language.'

example.hanzi: 他从未违背自己的诺言。
example.pinyin: tā cóng wèi wéibèi zìjǐ de nuòyán.
example.english: He has never broken his promise.
example.fact: The Hippocratic Oath, a promise physicians have taken for over two millennia, is traditionally attributed to the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates around the 5th century BC — most modern medical schools now use revised versions, since the original oath includes swearing by gods like Apollo and forbids surgery.

meanings: to sell at a reduced price

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拍 describes striking something lightly with the hand.
白 (bái) gives a sound distantly related to pāi, having drifted apart over time.
买 (to buy) — 卖 (to sell) is the flip side of buying, the other half of a transaction.
买 (mǎi) gives a sound very close to mài, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这幅画在拍卖会上卖出了高价。
example.pinyin: zhè fú huà zài pāimài huì shàng mài chū le gāo jià.
example.english: This painting sold for a high price at the auction.
example.fact: Leonardo da Vinci's painting Salvator Mundi sold at a Christie's auction in New York in 2017 for $450.3 million, making it the most expensive painting ever sold at auction — its attribution to da Vinci himself, rather than a student, is still debated by some art historians.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — cages and steaming baskets were traditionally woven from bamboo.
龙 (lóng) gives the sound — an exact match for 笼.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 那只鸟被关在笼子里。
example.pinyin: nà zhī niǎo bèi guān zài lóngzi lǐ.
example.english: That bird is kept in a cage.
example.fact: German animal dealer Carl Hagenbeck pioneered the 'barless enclosure' at his Hamburg zoo in 1907, replacing iron cages with moats and rockwork to give the illusion of animals roaming freely — his design influenced modern zoo architecture worldwide.

components.note: 买 is the simplified form of 買, traditionally written with 网 (a net) over 貝 (a cowry shell, used as ancient currency). The image of a net drawing in valuable shells gave 買/买 its meaning 'to buy, purchase.'
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 这套房子已经有买家了。
example.pinyin: zhè tào fángzi yǐjīng yǒu mǎijiā le.
example.english: This house already has a buyer.
example.fact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, buyers at the peak reportedly traded entire estates for a single rare tulip bulb before the market collapsed within weeks in 1637 — many economists cite it as one of history's earliest recorded speculative bubbles.

components.note: 囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.
土 depicts a mound of earth resting on the ground — a simple picture of soil, giving 土 its meaning 'earth, soil, land.'

example.hanzi: 保卫国土是每个公民的责任。
example.pinyin: bǎowèi guótǔ shì měi gè gōngmín de zérèn.
example.english: Defending the nation's territory is every citizen's duty.
example.fact: Russia is the largest country in the world by land area, spanning over 17 million square kilometers across eleven time zones — its territory is so vast that the sun rises in its easternmost region roughly ten hours before it rises in its westernmost region.

components.note: 已 began as a pictograph closely related to 巳, showing a coiled snake or a tied-off cord. The character was later borrowed phonetically to write the grammatical sense 'already, to stop, to cease,' unrelated to its original picture.
女 (woman) — 婚 relates to marriage, historically centered on the wife.
昏 (hūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 婚.

example.hanzi: 她现在已婚,有两个孩子。
example.pinyin: tā xiànzài yǐhūn, yǒu liǎng gè háizi.
example.english: She is now married and has two children.
example.fact: The oldest known written marriage contracts date back over 4,000 years to ancient Mesopotamia, where cuneiform tablets recorded dowries and property arrangements between families — historians consider these among the earliest surviving legal documents of any kind.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 憎 describes a strong inner feeling.
曾 (zēng) gives the sound — an exact match with 憎.
忄 (heart/mind) — 恨 describes a strong feeling in the heart, hatred.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound close to hèn.

example.hanzi: 他对不公正的现象充满憎恨。
example.pinyin: tā duì bù gōngzhèng de xiànxiàng chōngmǎn zēnghèn.
example.english: He is filled with hatred toward injustice.
example.fact: Neuroscientists using fMRI scans have found that intense hatred activates a distinct network of brain regions, including the putamen and insula, that partly overlaps with circuitry involved in romantic love — a 2008 study by University College London researchers first mapped this so-called 'hate circuit.'

components.note: 马 (horse) shows 驾 relates to driving or controlling an animal or vehicle.
加 (jiā) gives a sound close to jià, differing mainly in tone.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 请不要酒后驾车。
example.pinyin: qǐng bùyào jiǔhòu jiàchē.
example.english: Please do not drive after drinking.
example.fact: German engineer Karl Benz patented the first practical automobile powered by an internal combustion engine in 1886 — his wife Bertha Benz completed the first long-distance road trip by car in 1888, driving roughly 100 kilometers without her husband's knowledge to prove the vehicle's reliability.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 识's meaning 'to know, recognize,' knowledge conveyed through words.
只 (zhǐ) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shí.
另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.

example.hanzi: 这个软件可以识别人脸。
example.pinyin: zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ shíbié rénliǎn.
example.english: This software can recognize faces.
example.fact: Facial recognition technology traces back to the 1960s, when researcher Woodrow Wilson Bledsoe manually measured distances between facial features to test computer matching — modern systems now use deep neural networks trained on millions of images to identify faces in a fraction of a second.

components.note: 犭 (a beast, from 犬) — 狙 originally named a kind of ape or monkey.
且, in its less common reading jū, gives the sound — an exact match with 狙's reading.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 那名狙击手隐藏在屋顶上。
example.pinyin: nà míng jūjīshǒu yǐncáng zài wūdǐng shàng.
example.english: The sniper was hidden on the rooftop.
example.fact: The longest confirmed sniper kill on record was made in 2017 by a Canadian special forces soldier in Iraq, striking a target at a distance of 3,540 meters, over 3.5 kilometers away — a shot that required accounting for the Earth's curvature and the Coriolis effect caused by its rotation.

components.note: 土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.
辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過

example.hanzi: 他每天都会走过这条街。
example.pinyin: tā měitiān dōu huì zǒuguò zhè tiáo jiē.
example.english: He walks past this street every day.
example.fact: Yonge Street in Toronto was once listed in the Guinness World Records as the world's longest street at 1,896 kilometers, though the record was later revised after historians clarified that much of its length is actually Ontario's Highway 11 continuing north rather than Yonge Street itself.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.

example.hanzi: 我弟弟还在小学读书。
example.pinyin: wǒ dìdi hái zài xiǎoxué dúshū.
example.english: My younger brother is still in elementary school.
example.fact: Prussia introduced one of the world's first systems of compulsory elementary education in 1763, requiring children to attend school from around age five — the model influenced education systems across Europe and later the United States during the 19th century.

meanings: to settle (a dispute out of court)

components.note: 口 (mouth) — ties to harmony as speaking together in accord
禾 (hé, grain) gives the sound — matches 和's pronunciation hé
角 (horn) — 解 pictures removing a part of an animal.
牛 (ox) — together with a knife cutting between horn and ox, 解 pictures separating something into parts, giving its meaning 'to untie' or 'to explain.'

example.hanzi: 双方最终达成和解。
example.pinyin: shuāngfāng zuìzhōng dáchéng héjiě.
example.english: The two sides finally reached a reconciliation.
example.fact: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, established in 1995 under Archbishop Desmond Tutu, held public hearings where victims and perpetrators of apartheid-era violence could testify — perpetrators who fully disclosed their crimes could apply for amnesty, an approach later studied by other post-conflict nations.

components.note: 生 (a plant sprouting from the earth) — young green shoots gave 青 its association with a vivid blue-green color.
丹 (originally a well or a mineral pigment drawn from it) — paired with the plant above, it points to the mineral or plant-based dye that gave 青 its color meaning, later extended to 'young, youthful.'
虫 (small creature) — 蛙 names a small animal, grouped here alongside insects.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to 蛙's reading wā, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 池塘里有很多青蛙。
example.pinyin: chítáng lǐ yǒu hěn duō qīngwā.
example.english: There are many frogs in the pond.
example.fact: The golden poison frog of Colombia is small enough to sit on a fingertip, yet it carries enough batrachotoxin in its skin to kill about ten adult humans — indigenous Emberá people have traditionally used its toxin to coat the tips of blowgun darts.

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng

example.hanzi: 篝火里冒出无数火星。
example.pinyin: gōuhuǒ lǐ mào chū wúshù huǒxīng.
example.english: Countless sparks flew up from the bonfire.
example.fact: A single spark can be enough to ignite a wildfire under dry, windy conditions — investigators traced the 2018 Camp Fire in California, one of the deadliest wildfires in U.S. history, to a single faulty electrical transmission line spark.

components.note: 丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'
讠 (speech) — 误 began as a mistake in speech, later broadening to 'error' in general.
吴 (wú) gives a sound close to wù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 这次失误导致了严重的后果。
example.pinyin: zhè cì shīwù dǎozhì le yánzhòng de hòuguǒ.
example.english: This mistake led to serious consequences.
example.fact: NASA lost its $327 million Mars Climate Orbiter in 1999 because one engineering team used metric units while another used imperial units for a key navigation calculation — the mismatch caused the spacecraft to fly too close to Mars and disintegrate in its atmosphere.

components.note: 儿 (a standing person) — the figure being emphasized.
二 (an extra line at the top) — emphasizing the person's head, the 'first, foremost' part of them — the source of 元's meanings 'origin, first' and, by extension, the basic unit of Chinese currency.
糸 (thread) — plain, undyed silk thread
龶 — a plant stem, from which the raw silk thread hangs

example.hanzi: 氧气是一种重要的化学元素。
example.pinyin: yǎngqì shì yī zhǒng zhòngyào de huàxué yuánsù.
example.english: Oxygen is an important chemical element.
example.fact: Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev published the first widely recognized periodic table of elements in 1869, arranging elements by atomic weight and leaving gaps for elements not yet discovered — several of his predictions, including the properties of gallium and germanium, were confirmed within his lifetime.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 扑 describes striking or pouncing with the hand.
卜 shares a bilabial initial (b/p) with pū, though the rhyme has drifted from o to ū over time.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 他们晚上经常玩扑克。
example.pinyin: tāmen wǎnshang jīngcháng wán pūkè.
example.english: They often play poker in the evening.
example.fact: Playing cards are believed to have originated in China during the Tang dynasty around the 9th century, evolving from paper currency-like game sheets — they spread to the Islamic world and then to Europe by the late 14th century, where suits and face cards were later added.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 等 pictures bamboo strips, once used as writing tablets, being sorted.
寺 (originally a government office, later 'temple') — sorting and arranging bamboo documents at an official court gave 等 its meanings 'to wait,' 'rank,' and 'etc.'
亻 (person) — relates to 候's meaning 'to wait, time,' as if a person watching and waiting.
矦 (hóu) gives a sound hint — 候 is pronounced hòu, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 乘客们在站台上等候火车。
example.pinyin: chéngkè men zài zhàntái shàng děnghòu huǒchē.
example.english: The passengers waited on the platform for the train.
example.fact: In the 1990s, Disney popularized 'queue theming' — turning long waits into part of the entertainment by adding interactive scenery and storytelling along the line — after research showed that perceived wait time, not actual wait time, is what most affects visitor satisfaction.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, body) — 臀 (the buttocks) is a fleshy part of the body.
殿 (diàn) gives a sound only distantly related to tún today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).

example.hanzi: 长时间坐着会让臀部感到不适。
example.pinyin: cháng shíjiān zuò zhe huì ràng túnbù gǎndào bùshì.
example.english: Sitting for a long time makes the buttocks feel uncomfortable.
example.fact: The gluteus maximus, the main muscle of the buttocks, is the largest and one of the strongest muscles in the human body — anthropologists argue its unusual size compared to other primates evolved to stabilize the trunk during running, a trait linked to early humans' endurance hunting.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
戈 (a dagger-axe, a weapon) — 战 relates to fighting and war.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 战 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 第二次世界大战改变了世界格局。
example.pinyin: dì èr cì shìjiè dàzhàn gǎibiàn le shìjiè géjú.
example.english: World War II changed the global order.
example.fact: World War II, lasting from 1939 to 1945, is estimated to have caused between 70 and 85 million deaths worldwide, making it the deadliest conflict in human history — roughly 3 percent of the world's population at the time.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 露 names a form of moisture related to weather.
路 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 露.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 她的脸上露出了微笑。
example.pinyin: tā de liǎn shàng lùchū le wēixiào.
example.english: A smile appeared on her face.
example.fact: French neurologist Guillaume Duchenne identified in the 1860s that genuine smiles involve involuntary contraction of the muscles around the eyes, not just the mouth — this distinction, now called the 'Duchenne smile,' is still used by psychologists to distinguish authentic happiness from a posed expression.

components.note: 户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 房 is pronounced fáng, a close match
尸, here a variant of 厂, depicts a roof or shelter.
至 depicts arriving or coming to rest — settling under a roof gave 屋 its meaning 'house, room.'

example.hanzi: 地震摧毁了许多房屋。
example.pinyin: dìzhèn cuīhuǐ le xǔduō fángwū.
example.english: The earthquake destroyed many houses.
example.fact: Japan enforces some of the world's strictest earthquake-resistant building codes, requiring structures built after 1981 to withstand major seismic shaking without collapsing — after the 1995 Kobe earthquake killed over 6,000 people, many in older buildings, the codes were tightened further in 2000.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 编 originally described weaving or knitting threads together.
扁 (biǎn) gives a sound close to biān, with the tone shifted.
扌 (hand) — 排 relates to arranging things by hand into order
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to 排's reading pái, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 舞蹈老师重新编排了这支舞。
example.pinyin: wǔdǎo lǎoshī chóngxīn biānpái le zhè zhī wǔ.
example.english: The dance teacher rechoreographed this dance.
example.fact: Hungarian dance theorist Rudolf Laban developed Labanotation in the 1920s, a written system that records the timing, direction, and level of every body movement in a dance — it remains one of the primary methods choreographers use to preserve and reconstruct historical dance works.

components.note: Money/shell — greed is often about wanting money.
Gives the sound jīn, related to tān but drifted apart over time.
女 (woman) — 婪 (greed, avarice) is traditionally personified as a trait.
林 (lín) gives a sound distantly related to lán, sharing the initial consonant but having drifted apart in vowel over time.

example.hanzi: 贪婪常常使人失去理智。
example.pinyin: tānlán chángcháng shǐ rén shīqù lǐzhì.
example.english: Greed often makes people lose their reason.
example.fact: Squirrels are known to bury far more nuts and seeds than they can ever recover, a behavior called 'scatter hoarding' — studies show a single squirrel may cache several thousand nuts each autumn, and the ones it forgets often sprout into new trees, making squirrels unintentional forest planters.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 缩 describes thread pulling tight and shrinking.
宿 (sù) gives a sound close to suō.
八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'

example.hanzi: 这张图片可以缩小尺寸。
example.pinyin: zhè zhāng túpiàn kěyǐ suōxiǎo chǐcùn.
example.english: This image's size can be reduced.
example.fact: The Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, has shrunk to roughly a tenth of its original size since the 1960s after Soviet irrigation projects diverted the rivers that fed it — the exposed seabed is now a salt-and-dust desert known as the Aralkum.

components.note: 虍 (tiger) pictures a big cat.
业 pictures tall grass or a hilltop, together suggesting a hollow, empty den — giving 虚 its meaning 'empty, false.'
木 (wood) — 构 relates to building structures, originally from wooden framing
勾 (gōu) gives a sound close to 构's reading gòu

example.hanzi: 这个故事完全是虚构的。
example.pinyin: zhège gùshi wánquán shì xūgòu de.
example.english: This story is entirely fictional.
example.fact: In 1938, Orson Welles' radio adaptation of H.G. Wells' novel The War of the Worlds was presented as a series of simulated news bulletins about a Martian invasion — although reports of mass panic were later found to be exaggerated by newspapers, the broadcast remains one of the most famous examples of fiction blurring with perceived reality.

meanings: the limit of what one is prepared to accept

components.note: 广 (a building/shelter) — 底 relates to the base or bottom, as of a structure
氐 (dǐ) gives the sound — 底 is also pronounced dǐ, an exact match
纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.

example.hanzi: 诚实是他做人的底线。
example.pinyin: chéngshí shì tā zuò rén de dǐxiàn.
example.english: Honesty is his bottom line as a person.
example.fact: In 168 BC, Roman envoy Gaius Popillius Laenas drew a line in the sand around Seleucid king Antiochus IV and demanded he decide whether to withdraw from Egypt before stepping outside it — the ultimatum worked, and the phrase 'line in the sand' still describes a firm limit today.
